The spec viewer supports four security models: oneWayTLS_AppKey, oAuth, oneWayTLS_HMAC, mTLS_HMAC (bundle). · fetch curl

note: Quote: "Keys generated on Mastercard Developers are valid for 13 months." · Quick Start says reminders at '60, 30, 15, 5, and 1 day'; the OAuth Keys guide says '90, 60, 30, 15, 7, and 1 day(s)'. See contradictions.

claim: Production credentials are minted instantly at request time but stay inactive until Mastercard approves the production request; prerequisites are company verification, 'commercial countries' and a Business Relationship Type that covers the API.
title: Quick Start Guide | Platform Overview | Mastercard Developers
note: Quote: "Production credentials are generated instantaneously but they are only activated once your Production request is approved." · BRT doc (account-management/business-relationship-type/index.md): 'To request Production access, the API services added to your project must align with the BRT assigned to your company.' Missing BRTs are added via an emailed 'Customer Onboarding Platform' questionnaire; 'It may take up to 2 hours' to reflect. SSO customers skip company verification.

claim: Company verification on the developer portal is keyed to the Mastercard Company ID (CID) and pre-populates from the company's Mastercard Connect account, tying the developer portal to the gated client portal.
title: Company Verification
note: Quote: "If a corresponding Mastercard Connect account is found, the company data will be pre-populated." · CID is 'a 6-10 digit ID that Mastercard assigns to a business'. Verified accounts show a VERIFIED badge on My Account. Non-Connect customers enter company details and a request goes for manual review ('VERIFICATION IN PROGRESS'). · fetch curl

claim: OAuth 1.0a with RSA-SHA256 request signing is the default authentication scheme across the portal; OAuth 2.0 (FAPI 2.0) and mutual TLS are the two alternatives.
title: Authentication
note: Quote: "This is the default authentication mechanism used by most APIs on Mastercard Developers." · Page lists three protocols: OAuth 1.0a, OAuth 2.0 ('client credentials flow' plus FAPI 2.0), Mutual TLS (mTLS). No plain API-key scheme is offered. · fetch curl

claim: OAuth 1.0a mechanics: a 97-character non-secret consumer key plus a 2048-bit RSA private signing key (RSA only), signature method fixed to RSA-SHA256 with the oauth_body_hash extension; the portal can generate the key pair in the browser so Mastercard never holds the private key.
title: Using OAuth 1.0a to Access Mastercard APIs
note: Quote: "Consumer keys are 97-character identifiers for client applications consuming Mastercard APIs." · 'The signing key is a 2048-bit private RSA key'; 'It must be RSA-SHA256'. CSR doc: 'For OAuth 1.0a, only RSA keys are supported'. OAuth Keys guide: 'When you choose this option, your browser generates the private key and downloads it for you. Mastercard never sees your private key.' Keys are delivered as PKCS#12 (.p12). · fetch curl

claim: Mastercard's OAuth 2.0 is the FAPI 2.0 Security Profile: client authentication by private_key_jwt and sender-constrained access tokens via DPoP (ES256 or PS256), with a DPoP-Nonce handshake; sandbox token endpoint is sandbox.api.mastercard.com/oauth/token and example tokens live 900 seconds.
title: Using OAuth 2.0 to Access Mastercard APIs
note: Quote: "Mastercard implements the "FAPI2SP private key + DPoP" approach, which creates 2 layers of protection:" · Guide shows htu 'https://sandbox.api.mastercard.com/oauth/token' and a token response with '"expires_in": 900'. Only the sandbox token endpoint is printed; no production token URL found. OAuth Keys guide: 'For OAuth 2.0 keys, there is no rotate option. Instead, you add a new key and switch to it before the old one expires.' · fetch curl

claim: Auth scheme by service, as tagged in llms.txt: 73 services OAuth1.0a only, 7 OAuth1.0a and OAuth2 (FAPI 2.0), 5 MTLS, 5 NONE (documentation-only), 4 OpenBanking, out of 94 serviceId entries.
title: Mastercard Developers llms.txt
note: Quote: "authType: OAuth1.0a and OAuth2 (FAPI 2.0)" · Counts computed by grep of 'authType:' lines. MTLS services: Account to Account Commerce (CSP and DSP), Benefit Allocations Service (MTLS), Identity Insights for Accounts, Identity Insights for Transactions. · fetch curl

claim: For mTLS APIs there are two named hosts: an MTF sandbox at mtf.services.mastercard.com and production at services.mastercard.com; client certificates can be issued in seconds on the portal from a portal-generated or custom CSR, or obtained from the Key Management Portal inside Mastercard Connect.
title: Using mTLS to Access Mastercard APIs
note: Quote: "Sandbox mTLS certificates, which give access to an API sandbox that mimics a live Production environment (`mtf.services.mastercard.com`)" · 'Production MLTS certificates, which allow an application to access the Production environment (`services.mastercard.com`)'. 'The Key Management Portal (KMP) is an application available in Mastercard Connect' (link markup stripped). Uploading a certificate from an external CA is allowed 'ONLY ... if required by an API in your project'. · fetch curl

claim: REST base URLs are published per API and follow one pattern: sandbox.api.mastercard.com/<service> for Sandbox and api.mastercard.com/<service> for Production.

note: Quote: "Your client uses the Sandbox base URL: `https://sandbox.api.mastercard.com/bin-resources`." · Locations doc table lists 'Sandbox URL https://sandbox.api.mastercard.com/locations/atms' and 'Production URL https://api.mastercard.com/locations/atms'. Mastercom OpenAPI file lists server 'https://api.mastercard.com/mastercom' described as 'Global Production Server'. claim: Client-library deprecation policy: at least three months' notice via a GitHub 'maintenance | deprecated' label, then the repository is removed; supported runtimes are Java 17+, Node 19+, Python 3.9+, Go 1.20+, .NET Standard 2.1 and OpenAPI Generator 7.x.
title: Mastercard Versioning and Deprecation Policy (CLIENT_LIBRARY_DEPRECATION_POLICY.md)
note: Quote: "The notice is issued at least three months before the end-of-life date." · 'At the end of three months, we will remove the repository in which the depreciating version of the library resides.' Every SDK README links this policy. Fetched from raw.githubusercontent.com. · fetch curl

claim: API (service) deprecation has no fixed notice period: the policy says services are rarely decommissioned and the timeline varies product by product, communicated to affected customers with contractual terms.
title: Mastercard Versioning and Deprecation Policy (CLIENT_LIBRARY_DEPRECATION_POLICY.md)
note: Quote: "The timeline is often product and customer-impact dependent, so it varies from product to product." · Policy also warns that functionality 'may be changed without prior warning to patch a security vulnerability'. API versioning is per product (e.g. mastercom-v6, Account Validation spec versions 1.0.0 to 3.1.2); no portal-wide API versioning policy page was found. · fetch curl

note: Quote: "Download the OpenAPI Generator CLI (you can follow the instructions here)" · Link markup stripped from quote. Tutorial covers Java, Python, NodeJS and C#. claim: Outbound notifications are called webhooks and are product-specific: Transaction Notifications requires an HTTPS endpoint with mutual TLS, immediate HTTP 200 acknowledgement, and retries failed deliveries for up to 24 hours before parking them for 7 days.
title: Set Up Your Webhook (Transaction Notifications)
note: Quote: "Mastercard marks the delivery as failed and retries at progressive intervals for up to 24 hours." · 'Your endpoint supports mutual TLS (MTLS) authentication.' Webhook URLs are 'Register[ed] ... during onboarding', not self-service in the portal. Ethoca Alerts for Merchants likewise exposes a 'Push API (Webhook)' requiring 'MSSL (mutual SSL/TLS authentication)' and the DigiCert Assured ID Root G2 trust anchor. Commercial Event Notifications and Account-to-Account Commerce also document 'Webhook Notifications'. · fetch curl

claim: Open Finance US is consolidating its webhooks into a named subsystem, the Open Banking Webhook Management System (OBWMS), with existing services migrating during 2026; partners must allow-list about 30 published Mastercard source IP ranges.
title: Webhook Notifications (Open Finance US)
note: Quote: "Existing services will be migrated to the Open Banking Webhook Management System during 2026." · Webhook families: Data Connect, Data Connect Components, Report Webhooks, TxPUSH. claim: Rate limiting is enforced at the gateway on three axes (per IP, per service, per client) returning HTTP 429 with ReasonCode RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED, but the actual TPS ceilings are placeholders and never published.
title: OAuth 1.0a and mTLS Error Codes
note: Quote: "You have exceeded your rate limit. Maximum allowed: <max_client_tps> TPS." · IP limit: 'Maximum allowed: <max_ip_tps> TPS'; service limit: '<max_service_tps> TPS'. Errors are flagged 'Recoverable: true'. A gateway payload cap also exists: 'Payload too large. Limit: <max_payload_size> KB'. No Retry-After header is documented. · fetch curl

claim: Per-client call quotas are keyed to the first 48 characters of the consumer key and surfaced live in x-quota-current / x-quota-max / x-quota-period response headers; exceeding a quota returns HTTP 403 rather than 429.
title: OAuth 1.0a and mTLS Error Codes
note: Quote: "The quota period values can be `month`, `day`, `hour`, `minute` or `second`." · 'Client quotas will limit the number of calls that can be made per some time period with a particular consumer key.' Quota values themselves are not published. · fetch curl

claim: Sensitive fields are protected by an application-layer encryption scheme in addition to TLS: JWE compact serialization (RSA-OAEP, AES-CBC or AES-GCM) for field-level or whole-payload encryption, plus a legacy 'Mastercard encryption' format; open-source client-encryption libraries implement both.
title: Securing Sensitive Data Using Payload Encryption
note: Quote: "Mastercard uses JWE compact serialization for the encryption of sensitive data and supports both field level encryption and entire payload encryption." · Link markup stripped from quote. Legacy scheme 'involves an initialization vector, an encrypted or wrapped key, an encrypted value, a public key fingerprint and a digest algorithm' with RSA-OAEP SHA256/SHA512. Encryption certificates are issued per project via Credential Management. · fetch curl

claim: Change cadence is per product rather than portal-wide: Mastercard Send ships quarterly releases (26.2, 26.3, 26.4 scheduled) to MTF then Production, publishes release notes three months ahead, and freezes changes 23 Nov 2026 to 1 Jan 2027; other products keep a dated 'Release History' table.
